Speaker's Card/Request to Speak: If you would like to address the City Council on a scheduled agenda item, including a Consent Calendar item, a Regular Council Business item, a Public Hearing item, or Public Comments, please complete the "Request to Speak Form." The card is at the table at the entrance to the City Council Chamber. Please identify on the card your name and the item on which you would like to speak and return to the City Clerk. The "Request to Speak Form" assists the Mayor in ensuring that all persons wishing to address the City Council are recognized. It also ensures the accurate identification of meeting participants in the City Council minutes. Your name will be called at the time the matter is heard by the City Council. City policy is to limit public testimony to up to three minutes per speaker depending on relevant circumstances (unless the time limit is extended by the Mayor), which includes the presentation of electronic or audio visual information. Speakers may not yield their time to other persons.

NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv . For more information, please contact the City Clerk''s office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to a regular City Council meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk''s Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
1. Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting or at the time he/she addresses the City Council. Please provide 15 copies of the information to be submitted and file with the City Clerk at the time of arrival to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council at the time testimony is given.
2. Large Displays/Maps/Renderings:
Any member of the public who desires to display freestanding large displays or renderings in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to notify the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205 no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting so that an easel can be made available, if necessary.
3. Electronic Documents/Audio-Visuals:
Any member of the public who desires to display information electronically in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to submit the information to the Public Information Office (PIO) no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting. To facilitate your request contact the PIO Office at (949)724-6253 or the City Clerk''s Office at (949)724-6205.
Information must be provided on CD, DVD, or VHS; or, emailed by 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting to pio@ci.irvine.ca.us . Members of the public will be asked to provide their name, identify the meeting and the agenda item to be addressed, and a day time phone number.
The PIO office will notify the person submitting the information as soon as possible prior to the meeting if the information cannot be accessed or if the version provided is incompatible with the City''s system. Every effort will be made by City staff to facilitate the presentation.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE
Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesdays of each month at 4:00 p.m. Study Sessions and/or Closed Sessions are periodically held prior to the start of the regular meeting. Agendas are available at the following locations:
 City Clerk's Office
 Police Department
 Front Entrance of City Hall
 University Park Center (Culver/Michelson)
 Walnut Village Center (Culver/Walnut)
 Northwood Town Center (Irvine Blvd./Yale)
 City's web page at www.ci.irvine.ca.us

MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING

  April 23, 2019
  City Council Chamber
  One Civic Center Plaza
  Irvine, CA 92606

CALL TO ORDER
The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order at 4:15 p.m. on April
23, 2019 in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center Plaza,
Irvine, California; Mayor Shea presiding.
ROLL CALL
  Present:  4  Councilmember:  Melissa Fox
  Councilmember:  Farrah N. Khan
  Mayor Pro Tempore:  Anthony Kuo
  Mayor  Christina Shea

Following Roll Call, Mayor Shea noted that in the absence of a Closed Session, the
agenda would be reordered as follows: 1) announcements, 2) the Consent Calendar,
and 3) Council Business Item Nos. 4.1 through 4.4, with the remainder of agenda items
considered after 5 p.m.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE – IRVINE POLICE COLOR GUARD

Police Chief Hamel introduced the Irvine Police Color Guard and led the Pledge of
Allegiance.

INVOCATON

Pastor Jorge Molina from Mariners Church in Irvine provided the invocation.
 City Council Minutes  April 23, 2019

  1.  PRESENTATIONS

  1.1  Proclaim May 12-18, 2019 as "National Police Week"

  Mayor Shea introduced Mike Hamel, Chief of Police; Julia Engen, Assistant
  Chief of Police; Michael Kent, Police Commander; and members of the
  Irvine Police Color Guard, and presented a proclamation recognizing May
  12-18, 2019 as “National Police Week.”

  1.2  Young Master's Art Show 2019 Cover Artist

  Mayor Shea introduced Assistance League of Irvine President Jill Houskey
  and Art Teacher Liaison Mary Ann Breckenridge, as well as Heather Lee,
  fourth grade student from Portola Springs Elementary School, who was
  selected as the Young Master’s Art Show 2019 Cover Artist.

  1.3  Proclaim April 28 - May 5, 2019 as "Days of Remembrance"

  Councilmember Fox introduced Lisa Armony from Jewish Federation and
  Family Services Orange County, and presented a proclamation recognizing
  April 28 – May 5, 2019 as “Days of Remembrance.”

  1.4  Irvine Business Complex and North Irvine Transportation Mitigation
  Committee Project Status Update

  Jim Houlihan, Manager of Engineering/City Manager, and Melissa Dugan,
  Supervising Transportation Analyst, provided a brief status update on the
  Irvine Business Complex and North Irvine Transportation Mitigation
  Committee Project.

  1.5  Bristol Corridor Transit Study

  Eric Carlson, Orange County Fire Authority, provided a brief presentation to
  related to the Bristol Corridor Transit Study.

  1.6  Jamboree Pedestrian Bridge Update

  This item was removed from the agenda at the request of City Manager
  Russo. See Additions and Deletions.

  CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  There was no report; however, City Manager Russo requested that Item 1.6 (Jamboree
  Pedestrian Bridge Update) be removed from the agenda, noting that the item would
  return sometime in the fall. See Additions and Deletions.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Minutes  April 23, 2019

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Mayor Pro Tempore Kuo provided a brief update on volunteer efforts as part of the “1
  Million Hour Challenge” campaign, noting that over 15,000 volunteer hours have been
  logged to date by several members of the community, including Girl Scout Troop 3158,
  the Irvine Evergreen Chinese Seniors Association, and the Woodbridge Boosters; and
  announced that April was National Donate Life Month, noting the recent passing of
  community member Carolyn McInerney, and referred residents to donatelife.net for more
  information on organ donation.

  Mayor Shea provided a brief report on a recent meeting with Judge Carter’s office
  regarding the countywide homeless issue; and made the following announcements:

    One week remains to participate in the National Mayor’s Challenge for Water
  Conservation. This annual challenge to conserve water, sponsored by the Wyland
  Foundation in Irvine, reminds residents of the importance of this precious
  resource. To date, Irvine was among the top ten cities in its population category.
  To pledge to conserve water and other resources, visit mywaterpledge.com by
  April 30. For more information, visit cityofirvine.org.

    Time remains to participate in the Irvine Animal Care Center’s Virtual 5K to
  support animals in need. To participate, visit irvineanimals.org and complete a
  race (run or walk) at any location by April 30. A medal and certificate of
  completion will be mailed following participation. Four-legged friends are also
  eligible to participate and will receive a medal of their own. Proceeds go toward
  shelter and care for animals at the Center, which offers services such as licensing
  for Irvine residents, pet adoptions, and events. For information, visit
  irvineanimals.org/5K or call 949-724-7740.

    The City of Irvine has received the Excellence in Public Information and
  Communications Award by the California Association of Public Information
  Officials for Inside Irvine, the City’s quarterly magazine and activity guide. The
  award recognizes work that is innovative and has made a lasting impact on a
  community. Produced by the Public Information Office and the Community
  Services Department, Inside Irvine is mailed to all residents in Irvine, providing
  information on new and ongoing initiatives, future projects, special events,
  classes, and programs. The spring issue is now available at insideirvine.org, while
  the summer issue will be mailed to homes and available online on May 15.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council Minutes  April 23, 2019

  3.2  AMENDMENT TO THE ZONING ORDINANCE FOR ADMINISTRATIVE
  PROCEDURES FOR SMALL UTILITY FACILITIES

  Stacy Tran, Senior Planner, presented the staff report and responded to
  questions. Tim Gehrich, Deputy Director of Community Development, was
  also available for questions.

  Mayor Shea opened the public hearing at 6:38 p.m.

  The following individuals spoke in opposition to the proposed ordinance:

  Robert Jystad, Crown Castle
  Bridgett Pleasant

  Greg Smith, Planning Commission Chair Pro Tempore, spoke in favor of
  the ordinance, and reiterated that the proposed Ordinance would provide
  the City with maximum protection under the law.

  ACTION:  By consensus, Mayor Shea closed the public hearing at
  6:55 p.m.

  City Council discussion included: inquiring about health studies and
  regulations related to 5G towers and potential health impacts; questioned
  what the proposed ordinance would affirm; suggested a larger distance
  between 5G towers if possible on both larger and smaller streets; inquired
  about placing 5G towers in street medians; and inquired about a recent
  Supreme Court decision of April 4, 2019 (T-Mobile West vs. City and
  County of San Francisco), and whether that decision would have a
  favorable impact on the City of Irvine.

  City Attorney Melching noted that Federal law prohibits the City from
  considering any adverse health effects of wireless antennas, and confirmed
  that the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) is the regulatory
  authority and has such jurisdiction.

  ACTION:  Moved by Councilmember Fox, seconded by Mayor Pro
  Tempore Kuo, and unanimously carried to:

  Introduce for first reading and read by title only ORDINANCE NO.
  19-06 - AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  IRVINE, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING ZONE CHANGE 00771096-
  PZC TO AMEND THE ZONING ORDINANCE AND PROVIDE NEW
  CITYWIDE REGULATIONS FOR SMALL UTILITY FACILITIES

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  9

  Doug Eliot
  Kev Abazajian, Irvine resident
  Ellie Young, Irvine resident
  Laurel Davilla, Irvine resident
  Lauren Johnson-Norris, Irvine resident
  Joe McLaughlin, Irvine resident
  Lynn Woods, Irvine resident
  Ken Stahl, Irvine resident
  Ilya Tseglin
  Tim Steed, Orange County Employees Association

  The following individuals spoke in support of the appointment process:

  Scott Hansen
  Michael Carroll, Irvine resident

  City Council discussion included: inquiring about revisiting the list of
  candidates if no applicant received a majority vote; reiterated Municipal
  Code requirements to fill a vacancy; expressed concern about the cost of a
  special election and discussed the funding source; noted potential
  complexities with the appointment process; requested clarification of the
  City Clerk’s random selection process for scheduling interviews; suggested
  various appointment process guidelines and deadlines; suggested that the
  City Clerk conduct the random drawing in a public environment; questioned
  whether all applicants would be interviewed; and noted that deliberations
  could continue to the meeting of May 28 if consensus was not reached by
  May 14.

  ACTION:  Moved by Mayor Shea, seconded by Mayor Pro Tempore
  Kuo, to:

  1)  Allow each Councilmember to choose up to four individuals to
  interview.
  2)  Direct the City Clerk to conduct a random selection process in
  a public setting to determine the order of interviews.
  3)  Provide each candidate/applicant 15 minutes total, which
  includes their presentation and a City Council question/answer
  period, with phone interviews permitted for those who cannot
  attend in person; and politely request that interviewees not
  enter the Council Chamber until their scheduled interview.
  4)  Following interviews, allow each Councilmember to select 2-3
  finalists, which the City Clerk will list based on a random
  process as to who will be listed first, at which time the City
  Council will go down the list of finalists until a majority vote is
  reached.
